decision.title: The XML parser (packet )
decision.summary: The XML parser detects and transcodes encodings, walks the internal subset and content over explicit stacks of entity frames, bounds depth and entity expansion, and passes the whole W3C XML suite selection.

body.p: . src/xml.c (walk and checks), src/xml_encoding.c (encodings, character classes, positions), src/xml_entity.c (buffers, DTD tables with hash indices).

item.p: Decoding: Appendix F detection; UTF-8 and US-ASCII are parsed in place, UTF-16 and ISO-8859-1 are transcoded to a UTF-8 copy kept by the parser. UCS-4, EBCDIC and other names are UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE; an 8-bit document declaring UTF-16, a UTF-8 mark with another declared name, or BOM-less UTF-16 not declared UTF-16LE/BE is MALFORMED (4.3.3). U+0000 is refused before parsing (tree-sitter would read it as the end). Diagnostics give line, column (codepoints) and the input byte offset.

Walks without C recursion (): the internal subset, then the document's children, each over a stack of entity frames (cursor + tree) in allocator memory. A general entity in content is reparsed as <x>TEXT</x> (4.3.2); its tree is cached per entity for the parse; replacement text without < or & is sent as text without a parse. An internal parameter entity between declarations is included by parsing <!DOCTYPE d [TEXT]><d/> (2.8); conditional sections in it are not supported (the grammar has none). Entities in attribute values are expanded with an explicit stack (4.4.5). Element nesting is bounded by maximum_depth, expansion by maximum_entity_expansion_byte_count (every replacement text counted, parameter entities included).

Choices: line ends are normalized as text is emitted (pieces split at CR, the builder joins them), not in a copy; replacement text is not normalized again. Predefined entity names are always predefined (declarations of them are ignored). External parsed entities are skipped in content (4.4.3); undeclared ones are skipped when WFC Entity Declared does not apply. xml:id is an ID and collapsed; DTD types ID, IDREF(S) give is_id/is_idrefs. Element types and attribute names in DTD declarations must be QNames too. version 1.1 documents are parsed by the 1.0 rules, except that xmlns:p="" undeclares p (Namespaces 1.1, section 5). Unparsed entity system identifiers are passed as written, not resolved against the base URI.

Measured: W3C suite (Fifth Edition selection of ) valid 601/601, invalid 175/175, not-wf 948/948 through the library (tests/xml_conformance_test.c, which reads third_party/xmlconf from the source tree and passes with a "skipped" line where it cannot, as under WASI). Of the 9 NAMESPACE="no" valid/invalid tests, 8 are refused as not namespace-well-formed and counted as passing. QT4 suite: 1046 of 1051 *.xml files parse; the 5 refused are not well-formed on purpose (bad bytes, U+00BC in names, unknown encoding "foo", invalid-xml.xml). XSLT 4.0 suite, the 2541 files under 5 MB: 18 refused, 17 not well-formed on purpose and xml-version-03.xml, an XML 1.1 document with character references to control characters (1.0 rules apply).

CLI: sxml check (docs/CLI.md); the framework gains sxml_cli_file_reader in the invocation, implemented over stdio in apps/sxml/platform_stdio.c; CLI golden tests run in tests/cli/input/ so file names work under WASI too.
